summary: Iteration 5: Team members + Custom domain (Business plan features). Backend 9/9 pytest passed. Frontend UI verified: Settings shows team-members, custom-domain and billing cards; invite of a fresh email produces pending row; domain save reveals dns-instructions and verify button (verify -> 'failed' as expected). Workspace switcher visible for existingmate (2 workspaces), switch to Testify Demo loads its 6+ seeded testimonials, confirming get_user_workspace resolves the active workspace across all endpoints. Regression: overview + public /t/testify-demo still work.

minor.issue: Uses get_user_workspace() which respects active_workspace_id. If a user has switched to another workspace and then triggers onboarding, it will overwrite THAT workspace's name/branding and create a stray collection there. Was reproduced during testing (renamed Testify Demo to 'Mate Co' after existingmate had switched). Should target the workspace the user OWNS (owner_id == user.id) instead. Restored the seed manually.

action_items: Fix /api/onboarding to always update the user's OWNED workspace (owner_id == user.id) instead of get_user_workspace(user); otherwise a switched user can accidentally overwrite another workspace's identity.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown ~1330 lines; consider splitting into routers (auth, workspace, members, domain, payments) for maintainability.
/api/onboarding does not scope to owner-only workspace (see backend issue above).

workspace_members.delete_one on remove_member doesn't check whether the user is a member of THIS workspace before delete; harmless because no-op, but could return a misleading {ok:true} for non-members. Consider 404 if not found.
invite_member uses workspace_members.find_one to detect duplicates but does not consider case-normalized email uniqueness on the invites collection beyond upsert filter — acceptable for now.
Custom domain verify endpoint has no rate limit; a malicious owner could hammer DNS lookups. Consider rate_limit().
test_credentials: admin@testify.com/admin123 (Testify Demo owner, business), existingmate@example.com/pass123 (own workspace + Testify Demo admin). Onboarded flag set to true for mate during testing.
seed_data_creation: Fresh random-email invitees and one free-plan test user created via /auth/register. Testify Demo state restored (name='Testify Demo', no custom_domain, only admin+mate as members).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5.py. Existingmate account is now onboarded=true (previously false). Testify Demo restored to clean state. The onboarding endpoint bug reproduced above should be fixed before shipping onboarding changes; if fixed, re-run the entire test suite. Domain verify always returns 'failed' in this env (no DNS record) — expected.
rca of the issue: server.py:_owned_workspace-style handlers uniformly call authlib.get_user_workspace(user) which now returns the ACTIVE workspace (via active_workspace_id) rather than the OWNED one. /api/onboarding invokes this and then unconditionally overwrites name/primary_color/logo and creates a first collection. Reproduction: (1) login as existingmate (member of Testify Demo); (2) POST /api/workspaces/switch to Testify Demo; (3) POST /api/onboarding {business_name:'X'}; Testify Demo's name/logo are overwritten. Mitigation: in /api/onboarding, replace get_user_workspace with an owner-scoped lookup: `ws = await db.workspaces.find_one({'owner_id': user['id']})` and 404 if none.
